Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, this is the gate agent for flight eleven forty-two with service to New York Kennedy. We have been here at gate C nineteen since noon, and I know some of you have been waiting a long time, so here is where we stand. The aircraft has arrived, but the crew has not. They are coming in from Denver and they land in about twenty minutes. That means we start boarding at four fifteen, not at three forty. Two things before I go. One: this is a full flight, so if your carry-on does not fit in the overhead bin, we will check it at the door, free of charge. Two: if you have a connection in New York tonight, come and see me at the counter now, not after we board. I have done this job for nineteen years, and I can tell you, the line after boarding is the wrong line to be in.

Hi, this is Denise at the front desk, calling room eleven oh four. Two things, and then I will let you sleep. First, you asked about breakfast. It is complimentary for everybody on your rate, it is on the second floor, and it has run from six thirty to ten thirty since we reopened in March. Second, the concierge desk in the lobby closes at nine tonight, which is earlier than usual, so if you still want that table for tomorrow, come down before nine and ask for Ray. He has worked in this neighborhood for thirty years and he will get you in somewhere I could not. One last thing, and nobody ever tells you this: the express elevators do not stop on the second floor. You have to take the one by the gift shop. Guests have gotten that wrong since the day I started here.
